The visuals show a one-million-gem selection screen and a later email-entry screen, though they do not establish that the reward would be delivered or that both screens belong to one confirmed flow.

opening.argument: The evidence does not establish that any reward was actually delivered or that a viewer was guaranteed a result. The visible material stops at selecting an amount, with no shown completion, account credit, or confirmed transaction. Even the claimed tool is described in terms of what it could do, while the sampled sequence provides no independent confirmation. A careful viewer could therefore treat this as an unverified claim or demonstration rather than deceptive acquisition of an asset.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The title and description are certainly promotional, but promotion alone does not prove that the service is fraudulent. The cited language describes an alleged capability, and the visual evidence shows only an amount-selection screen. The reference argument itself concedes that delivery and even continuity between the screens are unestablished, leaving the central scam mechanism unproven.

opening.argument: The material can reasonably be read as an operational demonstration of a game-related tool and its interface. A tutorial label cannot convert an explicit purported acquisition mechanism into neutral commentary, even if the recording omits the final step.
